task: Golgi tendon organ (GTO) Ib force-feedback pathway -- the muscle FORCE sensor complementing muscle_spindle.py's Ia LENGTH sensor, distinct from the stretch-reflex arc. Three forced adversaries on the twin's own real soleus_r Hill-type curves + real 158-frame gait reconstruction: (A) active-vs-passive force-source dissociation (the decisive GTO-vs-spindle distinction), (B) autogenic Ib inhibition as an emergent, force-limiting closed loop, (C) state-dependent locomotor Ib reversal (fixed-sign model falsified against real gait data).

The mechanistic reality of autogenic Ib inhibition itself (claim B) is not in question; only its causal role in PNF's stretching benefit is contested by this specific source.

decorrelated_anchor.anchor_claim_A: Stephens, Reinking & Stuart 1975 (PMID 1177014) + companion Reinking, Stephens & Stuart 1975 (PMID 1177149) -- different lab, decade, and muscle (cat medial gastrocnemius) than Houk & Henneman/Houk & Simon 1967 (cat soleus); found and independently verified live THIS session, not present in the pre-existing script.
decorrelated_anchor.anchor_claim_B: Eccles, Eccles & Lundberg 1957 (PMID 13526123) -- direct intracellular electrophysiological demonstration of a real neural circuit (disynaptic IPSPs), independent of and decorrelated from the closed-loop force-fixed-point MODEL construct itself.
decorrelated_anchor.anchor_claim_C: Pearson & Collins 1993 (PMID 8229157, its own Ia-vibration dissociation control) + Duysens & Pearson 1980 (PMID 7370733, quantitative ~4kg threshold, semi-intact walking-cat preparation) + Conway/Hultborn/Kiehn 1987 and Gossard et al 1994 (fictive spinal-cat locomotion preparation) -- 2 independently decorrelated experimental preparations converge on the same reversal mechanism.

proposed_cell.claim: The Golgi tendon organ, in series at the muscle-tendon junction, encodes muscle FORCE (active tension far more sensitively than passive stretch -- the decisive distinction from the muscle spindle's length-sensing) and is the sensor for autogenic Ib inhibition (force-limiting, geometrically emergent from a monotonic transduction curve, gain-dependent in its high-force-preferential shape) and state-dependent locomotor Ib reversal (rest=inhibition, stance=excitation, load-reinforcing). Forced against the twin's own real soleus_r Hill-curves and real 158-frame gait reconstruction: the active-vs-passive dissociation and the locomotor reversal both survive forced adversaries anchored by 6 independently live-re-verified, decorrelated primary sources (2 found new this session); autogenic force-limiting is robust but its specific 'high-force-preferential' shape is gain-dependent, honestly partial, not fully confirmed at all tested gains.
